text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- ABB Schweiz announced its acquisition of the Grossenbacher Group's electro-installation sector as per July 1. The acquisition will make ABB leader among Swiss electronic installators.
- Belgian cartel officials approved the merger of Barry SA (France) with Klaus Jacob Callebaut AG (Zurich). The merger has made the firm the world's biggest cocoa bean processor.
- Zurich Insurance Group is acquiring a six percent stake or 4.023 million shares in the Polish bank Handlowy SA.
- Lucerne Cantonalbank is selling its subsidiary, travel agency Lukan Reisen AG, to Hotelplan in order to concentrate on its core business.
- Zug-based commodity trading group Glencore International AG (formerly Marc Rich) intends to acquire a 51 percent stake in Argentina's Oleaginosa Moreno, the world's biggest producer of edible oil.
- The number of welfare recipients in the Canton of Berne has risen by 94 percent since the start of the recession in 1990.
- Swiss watch and watch parts exports reached a record high of 3.1 billion Swiss francs in the first five months of 1997, a 5.6 percent rise over the same period in 1996.

- The number of overnight stays in Swiss hotels rose by 7.7 percent in May compared to May 1996. From January to May a total of 12.21 million overnight stays in hotels was registered, 2.2 percent more than the same period in 1996.
- Compagnie Financiere Richemont in Zug reported a 1996/97 operating profit increase of 19 percent to 954.2 million sterling.

- Rainer E. Gut, President of the Credit Suisse Group, gave a speech at the National Press Club in Washington on the subject of Switzerland's role in World War Two. Gut said he feels that the U.S. has been unfairly attacking Switzerland.
